channel.title: InfinityDB engineering notes
channel.description: How InfinityDB is designed, measured and built, gate by gate.

item.title: Why Vortex failed
item.description: InfinityDB started as a restart. Its predecessor had a SIMD parser, crash-point testing and a thousand-run concurrency lab, and still missed every target that mattered. It wasn't effort. It was the architecture.

item.title: Every failure is a seed
item.description: Time, randomness, disk and network are injected, so the whole node runs inside a simulator. When something breaks, one number replays it exactly.

item.title: Why this site has no benchmarks
item.description: Every public number needs replicates, a clean tree and the system we compare against in the same run. Until the ledger says Allowed, we say nothing.

item.title: Trust before the first tag
item.description: We moved the first public release back so every critical and high finding from the safety review could be closed red-first. Here is what changed, and why.

item.title: Documents as tape
item.description: JSON documents now live as a compact tape at every size. The memory gate failed, and the fix was to stop building a representation rather than tune it.

item.title: Durability belongs to the namespace
item.description: memory, everysec and always are three promises made by one log. The campaign that measured them also caught a real group-commit defect.

item.title: Architecture first: the M0 verdict
item.description: Before a single feature, an end-to-end skeleton had to clear hard STOP gates. The first verdict was no. This is how the gates, and the fabric, changed.
